messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — starting PRD draft for private deployment networking (customer-managed networking) for the Q2 roadmap. Main ask from our fintech pilot: full egress control, customer NAT/GW, dedicated BGP peering, DNS handoff. Need acceptance criteria, edge cases, and rollout gating. Anyone able to review by EOD Thu?

Kevin Patel: I can take network acceptance criteria. Quick starter list: support user-defined CIDR ranges; configurable NAT/GW (managed or customer-owned); BGP neighbor with MD5; route advertisement controls; deterministic fallback to hosted egress on failure.

Olivia Park: Add test plans for failover, bandwidth limits, MTU validation, and IPv6. Also call out cert rotation & TLS termination — we should NOT terminate customer traffic by default unless explicitly opted-in.

SRE Bot: Automated note: historical flake rate for on-prem BGP tests = 12%. Recommend canary size >= 2 tenants, and synthetic BGP churn tests in pipeline.

Maria Chen: Putting an acceptance-criteria snippet below — will add to RFC. Please comment on edge cases I missed.

Maria Chen: ```Acceptance criteria:
- Customer can inject/own primary egress NAT/GW or use Redwood-managed NAT.
- BGP session established with customer-controlled ASN; session uses MD5 and configurable hold timers.
- Routes advertised by customer are honored within expected convergence window (<= 30s under normal conditions).
- DNS handoff: customer-managed authoritative DNS remains source of truth; Redwood provides optional split-horizon guidance.
- No plaintext termination of customer traffic by default; TLS passthrough preserved unless customer requests TLS termination.
- Canary plan: 2 pilot tenants for 72h; automated e2e tests (BGP, egress, DNS, failover) must pass.
- Monitoring: NAT port utilization, BGP session flaps, route withdrawals, and latency SLO checks instrumented and alerting.```

Kevin Patel: Edge cases I want explicit coverage for: overlapping CIDR between customer and Redwood control plane; asymmetric routing when customer updates outbound filters; blackhole scenarios when customer withdraws routes mid-maintenance. Also NAT port exhaustion at scale — need soft limits and graceful 502 vs silent drops.

Olivia Park: Add split-horizon DNS edge: customer has internal names that resolve differently from public zone; we need runbook for split-horizon mismatch. Also proxies that rewrite TLS SNI or headers (3rd-party proxies) — impacts routing and certs. MTU path-discovery failure if IPsec is layered — include MTU checks.

Liam (Product Ops): Prioritization note: these are high-touch customer asks. Proposed scope for initial GA: support Redwood-managed NAT + optional customer-owned NAT via simple BGP peering and DNS handoff docs. Defer multi-region transit, full IPv6 dual-stack, and advanced policy routing to post-GA. Does that align?

Maria Chen: Yes, staged approach makes sense. Need explicit rollout gating: security review signed off, e2e perf within SLOs (p99 inference control-plane ops < 50ms extra), integration tests green, docs + runbook + support playbook. I'll draft PRD and tag reviewers.

Kevin Patel: @Olivia can you own the e2e perf test harness? @Liam can you confirm pilot customers for the canary?

Olivia Park: On it. I will simulate worst-case MTU and BGP churn, and add IPv6 smoke tests even if GA is IPv4-only.

Liam (Product Ops): I'll confirm two pilot customers by EOD Fri — fintech A is in, plus a healthcare customer that needs SOC2/ISO controls.

SRE Bot: Tracking: created ticket INF-7801 for networking acceptance tests and canary automation.

Maria Chen: Thanks all — I'll push initial RFC to #eng-platform later today and drop a short PRD link here. :thumbsup:

Kevin Patel: :thumbsup:

Olivia Park: LGTM, will review RFC when posted.

Liam (Product Ops): Thx, will coordinate stakeholders.

Maria Chen: small follow-up — call out metrics for NAT port failures and BGP flap counts as blocking for GA. Also we should document rollback plan if customer-managed routes cause service impact.

Kevin Patel: Agreed. I'll add rollback runbook draft to the RFC (bgp withdraw -> force egress to Redwood-managed NAT -> notify customer).

Olivia Park: I'll add perf gating thresholds to the PRD and include test harness runbook.

Maria Chen: Great. Will iterate and tag reviewers. End of thread.
